rules.title: Security Deposit Law - maximum deposit
rules.requirement: A landlord in New Jersey is not required to collect a security deposit, but if one is collected, it cannot exceed one and one-half times one month's rent, and yearly increases are capped at 10% of the current deposit.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless the tenant requests coverage in writing and 30 days pass.
rules.quoted_span:
The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than 
one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less. Any additional 
yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the dwelling is owner-occupied (2- or 3-family)

rules.title: Security Deposit Law - handling, investment, and interest requirements
rules.requirement: Landlords must hold security deposits in trust, not comingle them with personal funds, and deposit or invest the money in an interest-bearing account at a New Jersey bank or investment company depending on the number of units managed; deposits must be returned with accrued interest, including upon sale or transfer of the property.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords/designees receiving security deposit money for residential rental units in New Jersey, except seasonal rentals of 125 days or less.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to security deposits for seasonal use or rental of not more than 125 consecutive days.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord or designee who receives security deposit money for ten or less units must 
deposit that money in an insured bank or savings and loan association located in New Jersey in an 
interest-bearing account at the current interest rate at the time of deposit.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the rental is a seasonal use/rental of 125 days or less

rules.title: Security Deposit Law - court jurisdiction over disputes
rules.requirement: Security deposit disputes up to $5,000 (including penalties but not court costs) are heard in Small Claims; disputes over $5,000 but up to $15,000 go to the Special Civil Part of Superior Court.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to actions involving security deposits under New Jersey law.
rules.quoted_span:
The Small Claims section of the Special Civil Part of the Superior Court, Law Division in 
the county where the unit is located or in the county where the landlord resides has jurisdiction in 
actions involving security deposits where the amount does not exceed $5,000, including any 
applicable pena lties, but not including court costs.
